step1_analysis.description: A local sense amplifier or read evaluation circuit for an SRAM-based L2 cache. It uses an enable signal (LSA) to trigger the evaluation of small differential voltages on the bitlines (BT/BC) into full logic levels at the internal/output nodes.

paper_reference.title: A 4MB On-Chip L2 Cache for a 90nm 1.6GHz 64b SPARC Microprocessor

sense_delay.description: Delay from the sense amplifier enable signal (LSA) to the internal nodes resolving.

sky130_expected.calculation: Based on 1.8V supply and 0.5um channel lengths in the netlist, the delay will be larger than 90nm.
sky130_expected.reasoning: 0.5um length transistors in SKY130 will have moderate speed, yielding delays in the hundreds of picoseconds.

average_power.description: Average power consumption during a read operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_avg. With VDD=1.8V and typical switching currents of ~100uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A single sense amplifier consumes a small fraction of the total cache power.

min_bitline_differential.description: Minimum voltage difference between BT and BC required for correct sensing.

sky130_expected.calculation: Depends on transistor mismatch and threshold voltage variations.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical SRAM sense amplifiers require 50-100mV differential to overcome offset.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure sense delay and power consumption during a read operation.
